notes:
## React (software)
React (also known as React.js or ReactJS) is a free and open-source front-end JavaScript library that aims to make building user interfaces based on components more "seamless". It is maintained by Meta (formerly Facebook) and a community of individual developers and companies. According to the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, React is one of the most commonly used web technologies. Based on W3Techs, it is used by 6% of all websites.
React can be used to develop single-page, mobile, or server-rendered applications with frameworks like Next.js and React Router. Because React is only concerned with the user interface and rendering components to the DOM, React applications often rely on libraries for routing and other client-side functionality. A key advantage of React is that it – by default – only re-renders those parts of the page that have changed, avoiding unnecessary re-rendering of unchanged DOM elements. React is used by an estimated 6% of all websites.

## Vue.js
Vue.js (commonly referred to as Vue; pronounced "view") is an open-source model–view–viewmodel front end JavaScript framework for building user interfaces and single-page applications. It was created by Evan You and is maintained by him and the rest of the active core team members. Vue features an incrementally adaptable architecture that focuses on declarative rendering and component composition.

## Nuxt
Nuxt is a free and open source full-stack web framework based on Vue.js, Nitro, and Vite. Nuxt is inspired by Next.js, which is a similar framework based on React rather than the Vue JavaScript library.
The main advantage of Nuxt over using Vue alone is its universal rendering system. The framework works as both an in-browser single-page application (SPA) as well as a server-rendered static website, by "hydrating" a server-rendered page to a full SPA after it is loaded. This allows websites to have the search engine optimization and performance benefits of a server-rendered site in addition to the interactivity of a client-rendered application. Nuxt largely abstracts the server-rendering features from the developer, and it's therefore able to have a similar development experience to a traditional SPA using Vue's single-file component (SFC) system.
In addition to its universal rendering mechanism, Nuxt also provides many other benefits and quality-of-life features, such as path-based routing, hot module replacement (HMR), TypeScript support out of the box, and middleware and server logic.

## Web framework
A web framework (WF), web application framework (WAF), or web development framework is a software framework that is designed to support the development of web applications including web services, web resources, and web APIs. Web frameworks provide a standard way to build and deploy web applications on the World Wide Web. Web frameworks aim to automate the overhead associated with common activities performed in web development. For example, many web frameworks provide libraries for database access, templating frameworks, and session management, and they often promote code reuse. Although they often target development of dynamic web sites, they are also applicable to static websites.

plan.title: React vs Vue: Which Should You Learn First?
plan.description: A fair comparison of React and Vue for beginners, covering what each one is, how they differ, and who each suits best. Ends with a clear recommendation by situation.

beats.narration: You want to build modern websites, and everyone says to learn a framework first. But two names keep coming up: React and Vue. Pick wrong, and you lose weeks. So, which one?

Both help you build user interfaces from reusable pieces called components. We will compare them on four things: what they are, how they feel to learn, how big their ecosystems are, and who each one suits.
React is a free, open-source JavaScript library for building interfaces from components. It is maintained by Meta, formerly Facebook, together with a community of individual developers and companies.

props.definition: A free, open-source front-end JavaScript library for building user interfaces from components.
props.origin: Maintained by Meta and a community

beats.narration: Vue, pronounced like the word view, is a JavaScript framework for interfaces and single-page applications. It was created by Evan You, and he maintains it with the rest of the active core team.

props.definition: An open-source front-end JavaScript framework for building user interfaces and single-page applications.

beats.narration: Here is a key difference in design. React only handles the interface and rendering components. For things like routing, you usually add other libraries. Vue calls itself incrementally adaptable, so you can adopt it a piece at a time.

React has a smart habit. By default, it re-renders only the parts of the page that have changed, avoiding unnecessary updates of elements that stayed the same. That keeps interfaces responsive as they grow.

Vue focuses on declarative rendering and component composition. You describe what the page should look like, and you build it by combining small components. That idea is the same one React teaches, just in a different style.

Both also grow into full applications. React pairs with frameworks like Next.js and React Router. Vue has Nuxt, which is inspired by Next.js and adds server rendering, path-based routing, and TypeScript support out of the box.

Now for reach. According to the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, React is one of the most commonly used web technologies. That matters, because popular tools usually mean more tutorials, more answers, and more job listings.

props.label: of all websites use React, per W3Techs

beats.narration: Vue is smaller in reach, but it is far from niche. It is led by one creator and a dedicated core team, which gives the project a clear direction and a consistent style.
Be careful with one thing, though. Neither choice is a dead end. Components, state, and rendering are shared ideas, so what you learn in one carries over to the other when you need to switch.

props.text: The ideas you learn carry over to the other one.

beats.narration: If you want the widest reach, pick React. It is backed by Meta, widely used across the web, and it opens the door to mobile and server-rendered apps through its surrounding frameworks.

If you want a gentler on-ramp, pick Vue. You can adopt it incrementally, and its single-file components keep things together. Nuxt then adds server rendering later, without changing your everyday workflow much.

props.heading: Pick Vue if you want
items: To adopt it step by step

beats.narration: So here is the honest answer. It depends on your goal. Chasing jobs and reach? Start with React. Want a smoother, incremental start? Start with Vue. Either way, build one small project this week.

props.text: Pick one, build something this week, and keep going.
